latest_reply.text:
Both corrections are committed on my branch (1353cc30) and nowhere else: nothing is merged, pushed or built. The merge hold stays.

**Where a failed read turned into "lost writes":** `serviceDrill` in `scripts/verify-serverless-local.mjs`, in two places. After each write phase, `listed` is built from b's `findDocs` result, falling back to an empty string when that call fails. After the SIGTERM, `kept` is built the same way, and the failure message shows `vanished` in place of b's error whenever anything counts as missing. Both now record a failed read as "findDocs on b failed, survivors unknown" with b's actual error. Writes count as missing only when they're absent from a listing that succeeded.

**The try_create_lock change:** the fallback treated any `Io` error from its exclusive create as "lock held". Now only an existing entry counts as contention, and every other create error is returned. The browser host sends a raw `-17` for an existing entry (`src/browser/host-vfs.mjs:33`), which std can't classify on wasm, so I match 17 explicitly on that target only. That's what kept the host path working under the old rule.

**Ownership:** no other branch or open thread touches `write.rs` or the serverless lane script. The SMB lock and Floci threads are resolved, and develop's only change since my rebase is a docs commit.

**Still pending validation:** rustfmt passes and the script parses. Clippy, the storage tests (including wasm) and prettier haven't run, because they need the Surface.

**The missing observation is still b's `findDocs` result after the SIGTERM.** If the stuck comparison run finishes, it still has the old drill, so its log shows that result only if nothing counts as missing.

threads.title: Cloud Run and Azure Functions emulation

latest_status.text:
Fix the NFS stale-attribute write failure

✓ Found it: the before-image capture stats the path, which NFS answers from cache
✓ Changed the EFS profile to take metadata from the opened file instead
✓ NFS 4.1 lane now passes alternating writers with default caching
✓ New EFS-lane step fails without the fix and passes with it
✓ Storage and machine tests, clippy and fmt pass (one root-only test fails on develop too)
**✓ Merged into develop (913c5db)**

latest_reply.text:
Fixed and merged into develop ([913c5db](https://github.com/d31ma/FYLO/commit/913c5db5)).

- **Fix:** before taking a before-image, the EFS profile now reads the file's timestamp from the opened file. Opening forces NFS to refresh its cached attributes, so it no longer trusts the stale path lookup.
- **NFS 4.1 lane:** two instances writing in turn now pass with default caching.
- **EFS lane:** it now alternates writers between two NFS clients. I confirmed this new step fails with the old code (same "timestamp changed" error) and passes with the fix, so CI will catch it if it comes back.
- **Tests:** storage and machine tests, clippy and fmt pass on the Surface. One permissions test fails because the build container runs as root, and it fails on develop the same way. In my first test run, 7 invocation tests also failed once; they passed in the three runs after that, so I'm treating it as load flakiness.

Three smaller findings are still open: hard-link errors not reaching FYLO's fallback, SMB reporting a lock conflict as a permission error, and the Floci lane's lock file sitting outside EFS.

latest_assistant.text:
The fix is merged into develop as 913c5db and pushed. FYLO no longer fails writes when two instances write in turn on NFS 4.1. This mattered beyond Azure because EFS runs on the same NFS client behaviour, so Lambda deployments were exposed too.

- **Cause:** before taking a before-image of a file, FYLO read its timestamp with a path lookup. NFS can answer that from a cache that is stale after the other instance's write, so the timestamp didn't match the opened file. About a third of alternating writes failed with "private copy source timestamp changed".
- **Fix:** the EFS profile now reads the timestamp from the opened file, because opening forces NFS to refresh it. The change is in `crates/fylo-storage-native/src/write.rs`.
- **EFS lane (`bun run efs:local`):** it now alternates writes between two NFS clients. That step fails with the old code and passes with the fix, so CI will catch it if it comes back.
- **Azure Files over NFS 4.1:** the two-instance writes that used to fail now pass with normal caching.
- **Tests:** the storage and machine crate tests, clippy and fmt pass on the Surface, with one exception. A file-permissions test fails because the build container runs as root, and it fails the same way on develop. In my first run, 7 invocation tests also failed once; they passed in the three runs after that, so I'm treating it as load flakiness.

Three smaller findings from the emulation work are still open:
- **Hard-link fallback:** gcsfuse and SMB refuse hard links with errors FYLO's fallback doesn't recognise, so every write fails on those mounts.
- **SMB lock conflicts:** SMB reports a lock conflict as a permission error. A second instance therefore fails instead of waiting for the root.
- **Floci lock file:** the lane's lock file sits outside the EFS mount. Moving the root inside the mount breaks the lane, so I left it as it was.

threads.title: Floci lock file on EFS

latest_status.text:
Move Floci lock file onto EFS

✓ Found it: the lane overrides the root to the mount point itself
✓ Moved the root to /mnt/state/root; the Lambda example creates it
✓ Lane now asserts the lock file is on the EFS volume
✓ Full efs:local lane passed on the Surface (693 s)
**✓ Rebased on the SMB fix and merged into develop (c388bc0)**

latest_reply.text:
I've fixed it and merged it into develop ([c388bc0](https://github.com/d31ma/FYLO/commit/c388bc05)). There's no PR.

- **Cause:** the Floci lane set the root to the EFS mount point itself. FYLO keeps the root's lock file beside the root, so the lock landed in the container's own `/mnt`, outside EFS.
- **Fix:** the root is now `/mnt/state/root`. The Lambda example creates that directory on cold start, which is what failed with `ENOENT` last time. Concurrent invocations now contend on a lock that lives on EFS, and the concurrent-write step still commits both writes.
- **New check:** the lane now confirms the lock file is actually on the EFS volume. I didn't run the old setup against it to watch it fail.
- **Lane result:** the full `efs:local` lane passed on the Surface in 693 s, using the Surface's own cache dir instead of the Mac path from the brief. Every step passed: crash suite, cross-client drill, and Floci Lambda.

I rebased onto the SMB lock-conflict fix before merging, and the qualification doc now marks this finding fixed.

latest_assistant.text:
The Floci test lane's lock file now sits on the EFS mount, and the full `efs:local` lane passes with the change. I merged it into develop (c388bc0) and pushed develop, with no PR. The SMB lock-conflict fix had already landed on develop, so I rebased onto it first.

- **Cause:** the lane used the EFS mount point itself as FYLO's root. FYLO puts the root's lock file next to the root, so it ended up in the container's own `/mnt`, outside EFS.
- **Fix:** the root is now `/mnt/state/root`, and the Lambda example creates that directory when it cold-starts. Last time, moving the root failed with `ENOENT` because nothing created that directory.
- **New check:** the lane now confirms the lock file is actually on the EFS volume. Concurrent invocations now compete for that lock on EFS, and both concurrent writes still commit. I didn't run the old setup to watch the new check fail.
- **Lane result:** the full lane passed on the Surface in 693 s, covering the crash suite, the cross-client drill and the Lambda step in Floci. I used a cache directory on the Surface rather than the Mac `/Volumes/ANNEX` path in your command.
- **Untested combination:** that lane run was before the rebase, so the merged tree with the SMB fix hasn't been through the lane. The SMB change is in the lock error handling and I don't expect it to affect this lane.

The qualification doc now marks this finding as fixed. Project memory now lists only the hard-link fallback as an open finding and records the Surface setup steps for this lane.

threads.title: Disk-full recovery check
threads.title_source: task label from previously inspected session; current UI title unverified

latest_status.text:
Disk-full recovery check

✓ Reproduced "write failed and rollback failed" on a 4 MB test disk (Surface)
✓ Found the gap: reads stay stuck on "concurrent write" after a failed rollback or crash
✓ Fixed: a stuck read now recovers the stranded write and retries
✓ Disk-full sweeps clean: 101 runs, 0 failures, no manual recover
✓ Crash matrix (270 recoveries), clippy, fmt and machine tests pass
**✓ Merged into develop and pushed**

latest_reply.text:
Nothing is needed from you. FYLO's data survived a full disk, but reads stayed stuck afterwards, so I fixed that and merged the fix into `develop`.

**What I found:** I filled a 4 MB test disk on the Surface at every point during a write. The "write failed and rollback failed" error showed up for puts, patches, deletes and SQL. No data was lost: once space was freed, an explicit recover or the next write repaired the store every time. Until one of those happened, though, every read failed with a false "concurrent write" error. A crash mid-write left reads stuck the same way. The existing crash test missed this because it always ran recover before reading.

**The fix:** when a read finds a write that nothing is finishing, it now finishes the repair itself and tries the read again. The crash test now also reads before recovering.

**Checked on the Surface:** 101 disk-full runs with 0 failures and no manual recover, plus the crash test (all 270 interrupted writes recovered), clippy, fmt and the machine tests. The Mac was never used.

Reads still fail while the disk is actually full, because the repair needs space. They work again as soon as space is freed. I haven't run the disk-full test on macOS because the benchmark thread asked me to keep off the Mac.

latest_assistant.text:
FYLO recovered its data after the disk filled. Reads stayed stuck afterwards, though, so I fixed that and merged the fix into `develop`.

- **What happened when the disk filled:** I filled a 4 MB test disk on the Windows Surface at every point during puts, patches, deletes and SQL writes. The "write failed and rollback failed" error showed up, because the rollback also needs disk space.
- **No data was lost:** once space was freed, running `recover` or making the next write repaired the store every time.
- **What was broken:** until that happened, every read failed with a false "concurrent write" error. A crash mid-write left reads stuck the same way. The existing crash test missed this because it always runs `recover` before it reads anything.
- **The fix:** when a read finds a write that nothing is finishing, it now finishes the repair itself and tries the read again. This only runs after a read has already failed, so normal reads are no slower.
- **Test change:** the crash test now also does a read before running `recover`, so this case is covered on every platform.

On the Surface, 101 disk-full runs passed with no `recover` step. The crash test recovered all 270 interrupted writes. Clippy, fmt and the machine tests also pass.

Reads still fail while the disk is actually full, because the repair needs space, and they work again once space is freed. I didn't run anything on the Mac, so the disk-full test hasn't been run on macOS.
